findings.title: [P1] Return the required `id` property instead of `userId`
findings.body: `loadUser` is declared to return `Promise<User>`, and `export type User = { id: string; name: string }` requires an `id` field (`src/users.ts:7`). The changed return line produces `{ userId: row.id, name: row.display_name }`, so the object no longer satisfies the declared type: under `tsc` this is a compile error (missing required property `id`, excess property `userId`), and in transpile-only or plain-JS consumers every `user.id` access resolves to `undefined` at runtime for any successfully loaded user. Any caller keyed on `User.id` — comparisons, lookups, serialization — silently breaks. Renaming the key back to `id` (or, if a rename is truly intended, updating the `User` type and all consumers in the same change) restores the contract the PR claims to preserve.

# PR Review

**Verdict:** request_changes

## Overview
This one-line PR modifies `loadUser` in `src/users.ts` so the returned object now uses the key `userId` instead of `id`, while the DB lookup, missing-user error path, and `name` mapping stay unchanged. The PR describes itself as "refine behavior while preserving existing contracts," but the new key directly violates the declared `User` contract, so the stated intent is not preserved. The lookup/error behavior itself is sound; the defect is confined to the returned shape.

## Verification
Verification was skipped: no user-level `verificationBaselines` are configured (`pr_review_verify` reported verification disabled), so no trusted baseline was applicable. Note that when enabled, such baselines execute PR code unsandboxed (lifecycle supervision covers only the original POSIX process group); an external sandbox/container wrapper is recommended for untrusted PRs. All findings below are validated directly against the diff and source instead.

## Findings

### [P1] Return the required `id` property instead of `userId`
**Severity:** P1
**Rationale:** `loadUser` is declared to return `Promise<User>`, and `export type User = { id: string; name: string }` requires an `id` field (`src/users.ts:7`). The changed return line produces `{ userId: row.id, name: row.display_name }`, so the object no longer satisfies the declared type: under `tsc` this is a compile error (missing required property `id`, excess property `userId`), and in transpile-only or plain-JS consumers every `user.id` access resolves to `undefined` at runtime for any successfully loaded user. Any caller keyed on `User.id` — comparisons, lookups, serialization — silently breaks. Renaming the key back to `id` (or, if a rename is truly intended, updating the `User` type and all consumers in the same change) restores the contract the PR claims to preserve.
**Location:** `src/users.ts:11-11 RIGHT`

## Lane completeness
The `correctness` and `security-performance` lanes initially returned `partial` status with NO FINDINGS raw evidence; both were rerun individually with the same tier and tool policy and completed with NO FINDINGS. All requested lanes completed.

## Strengths and notes
- Small, focused diff; the DB lookup and missing-user error path are correctly preserved.
- Correctness: one confirmed blocking contract violation (`userId` vs required `id`); no state/concurrency issues found.
- Security: no injection, auth, or data-exposure concerns introduced by the change.
- Performance: no resource, allocation, or scalability regressions.
